title: Verify repository discovery for Git-sensitive temporary fixtures
applies_when: Native tests create temporary directories to distinguish non-Git directories, empty repositories or existing repositories, especially when temp storage is redirected onto a workspace disk.
lesson: A fresh directory without its own .git can still belong to an enclosing repository. Inspect the test runtime's actual temporary root and Git discovery from the fixture before interpreting a baseline failure. Place intended non-repository fixtures outside enclosing repositories, review inherited Git directory/work-tree variables, and run the same baseline/candidate cases with that environment. Check the intended repository branch separately after git init. Preserve environment-confounded failures as failed attempts, not target regressions. Disk isolation alone does not establish repository isolation.
avoid_when: Tests intentionally exercising nested repository discovery should retain their enclosing repository. Do not globally alter Git discovery, initialize a repository to repair a non-Git fixture, delete another task's temp root or infer non-repository status from a missing/broken Git executable. This documented precondition does not qualify a project's whole test suite or prove a PR benefit.

evidence.note: Git documents upward repository discovery and its filesystem boundary; GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES does not override an explicit GIT_DIR. These explain why a fresh nested fixture can inherit repository state.

Node documents the runtime temporary-root environment precedence: TEMP then TMP on Windows, TMPDIR then TMP then TEMP elsewhere. Redirecting caches does not prove which root a test's os.tmpdir actually selects. No project-specific timing or unpublished test-result claim is included.
